title: Completing the Rewrite from Hell: Five Years of Technical Debt and How We Escaped - Aaron Stannard
summary: Aaron Stannard's SDKbin post-mortem: unreviewed microservice and generic-repository architecture, fake test coverage, and a strangler-fig recovery with ADRs and AI help.

assertions.quote: For a twoperson team, you do not need this.
It produced n plus1 queries everywhere

verdicts.note: A commonly documented .NET anti-pattern; the problem is the abstraction's inflexibility rather than inevitability.

assertions.quote: I could have figured this out that there was a problem in about 10 minutes.

verdicts.note: Early structural decisions are the costliest to reverse, though the exponential defect-cost curve behind this is overstated.

assertions.quote: we effectively had a test suite that told us nothing about how well our codebase worked
You've got to make sure they can narrate it back to you and understand the reasoning

verdicts.note: Read-back is standard in safety-critical communication; software evidence is anecdotal.

assertions.quote: We had to abandon that because the integration risk with the old billing system was just way too high.
the code that is already in the codebase is like the strongest center of gravity for what the AI is going to infer

verdicts.note: Consistent with how code models condition on context; measured mainly in practitioner reports.

assertions.quote: That is not something I would recommend as your primary testing strategy because it's very brittle.

verdicts.note: Matches the test-pyramid rationale; brittleness of UI tests is well documented.

assertions.quote: the sort of culture of writing things down and explaining why we did stuff is just as valuable for people as it is for LLMs

verdicts.note: ADRs are widely adopted; the benefit is reported, not measured.
